benefits.name: Electricity Rebate
benefits.summary: A yearly rebate of about $399 off your home electricity bill.
benefits.eligibility_text: Queensland Seniors Card, Pensioner Concession Card (Services Australia or DVA), Health Care Card or Veteran Gold Card. Must be the electricity account holder at your principal place of residence; one rebate per household. CSHC holders are not eligible.
benefits.value_text: $399.47 a year (GST inclusive)
benefits.how_to_claim: Phone your electricity retailer with your concession card; it is then deducted from your bills.
benefits.notes: Page does not name the rebate year. Commonwealth Seniors Health Card on its own does not qualify (Qld Seniors Card does).

benefits.name: Reticulated Natural Gas Rebate
benefits.summary: A yearly rebate of about $96 off your piped natural gas bill.
benefits.eligibility_text: Queensland Seniors Card, Pensioner Concession Card or Veteran Gold Card (Health Care Card is electricity-only). Must be the gas account holder at your principal place of residence.
benefits.value_text: $96.45 a year (GST inclusive)
benefits.how_to_claim: Contact your gas retailer; the rebate is deducted from your bills.
benefits.notes: Not for bottled LPG.

benefits.name: Electricity and Gas Rebates for Home Park and Multi-Unit Residents
benefits.summary: If your power comes through a park, village or unit-complex owner, you still get the rebate as a daily amount.
benefits.eligibility_text: Residents of residential parks, multi-unit complexes, granny flats etc. who are billed by a proprietor and hold a Qld Seniors Card, PCC, Health Care Card (electricity only) or Veteran Gold Card. Principal place of residence only; not nursing homes, motels or dormitories.
benefits.value_text: Electricity $1.0945 a day (incl GST); gas $0.2643 a day (incl GST)
benefits.how_to_claim: Ask your park owner or proprietor to add you to their Form 502 application to the energy retailer.
benefits.notes: Daily electricity rate works out to about $399 a year; you do not hold the account yourself, so 'electricity_account' is approximate.

benefits.name: Home Energy Emergency Assistance Scheme (HEEAS)
benefits.summary: One-off help of up to $720 to pay an electricity or gas bill after an emergency or money crisis.
benefits.eligibility_text: Responsible for the overdue bill and hold a concession card, or have income at or below the part-age-pension limit, or be on your energy retailer's hardship program; plus a big drop in income or high unexpected essential costs in the last 12 months.
benefits.value_text: Up to $720, once every 2 years
benefits.how_to_claim: Ask your energy retailer for an assessment and application number, then apply online at heeas-application-form.treasury.qld.gov.au.
benefits.notes: One-off payment so max_annual_value is null. Card list is broad because the page says 'a current concession card' or income test.

benefits.name: Medical Cooling and Heating Electricity Concession Scheme
benefits.summary: About $522 a year towards power bills if a medical condition means you must heat or cool your home.
benefits.eligibility_text: PCC (Services Australia or DVA) or Health Care Card; financially responsible for the electricity bill; a specialist certifies a condition such as MS, autonomic dysfunction, loss of sweating capacity or temperature hypersensitivity.
benefits.value_text: $522.09 a year (incl GST), paid quarterly to your bank
benefits.how_to_claim: Fill in the MCHECS form with your specialist and post it.

benefits.name: Electricity Life Support Concession (Oxygen Concentrator)
benefits.summary: About $1,063 a year towards the power used by a home oxygen concentrator.
benefits.eligibility_text: Oxygen concentrator supplied free through the Medical Aids Subsidy Scheme, and hold a Pensioner Concession Card, Health Care Card or Queensland Seniors Card.
benefits.value_text: $1,063.30 a year per machine, paid quarterly
benefits.how_to_claim: Complete the form MASS sends within 14 working days of getting the machine.
benefits.notes: Page shows 1 July 2025 rates; 2026-27 rate not shown.

benefits.name: Electricity Life Support Concession (Kidney Dialysis)
benefits.summary: About $712 a year towards the power used by a home kidney dialysis machine.
benefits.eligibility_text: Home dialysis machine supplied free by a Queensland Health hospital. No concession card requirement is listed.
benefits.value_text: $712.07 a year per machine, paid quarterly
benefits.how_to_claim: Complete the form from your hospital Renal Unit.

benefits.name: Pensioner Rate Subsidy
benefits.summary: 20% off your council rates, up to $200 a year.
benefits.eligibility_text: Pensioner Concession Card (Services Australia or DVA) or DVA Gold Card; owner or life tenant of your principal place of residence in Qld and legally responsible for the rates.
benefits.value_text: 20% of gross rates and charges, up to $200 a year
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply through your local council.
benefits.notes: Many councils add their own extra pensioner rebate; not covered here.

benefits.name: South East Queensland Pensioner Water Subsidy
benefits.summary: Up to $120 a year off water charges for pensioner homeowners in South East Queensland.
benefits.eligibility_text: PCC (Centrelink or DVA) or DVA Gold Card; own or have a life tenancy in your principal place of residence in the SEQ Water Grid and be responsible for rates and charges.
benefits.value_text: Up to $120 a year
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply to your water retailer (e.g. Urban Utilities, Unitywater or your council).
benefits.notes: Page is old (2017); confirm amount with retailer. SEQ only.

benefits.name: Emergency Management Levy Concession
benefits.summary: 20% off the Emergency Management Levy on your council rates notice.
benefits.eligibility_text: Commonwealth Pensioner Concession Card or Repatriation Health (Gold) Card; principal place of residence.
benefits.value_text: 20% off the Emergency Management Levy
benefits.how_to_claim: Ask your local council (often applied with the rates subsidy).
benefits.notes: Dollar value depends on property levy class.

benefits.name: Home Assist Secure
benefits.summary: Help with the labour cost of essential small home repairs and safety jobs, up to $500 a year.
benefits.eligibility_text: Aged 60+ (or any age with a disability), hold a Pensioner Concession Card, and unable to do the work yourself. Homeowners and renters. Usually not if you get Commonwealth Home Support or Support at Home.
benefits.value_text: Labour subsidy up to $200 a job and $500 a year (jobs up to $1,500 total)
benefits.how_to_claim: Contact your local Home Assist Secure provider (search by suburb or call 13 QGOV); they visit and arrange the work.
benefits.notes: Smoke alarm $250 component has ended in some areas.

benefits.name: Queensland Seniors Card
benefits.summary: A free card giving access to state concessions and business discounts for older Queenslanders.
benefits.eligibility_text: Permanent Qld resident living in Qld 6+ months a year; aged 65+ working under 35 hours a week, or 60-64 working under 35 hours a week and holding a PCC, Health Care Card or DVA Gold/White/Orange card.
benefits.value_text: Free card; unlocks concessions and discounts
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply online, by phone on 13 QGOV, in person at a Qld Government Service Centre, or by post.
benefits.notes: Age 60-64 without a card: Seniors Business Discount Card only.

benefits.name: Seniors Card +go
benefits.summary: Your Seniors Card with a built-in go card for South East Queensland public transport.
benefits.eligibility_text: Eligible for a Queensland Seniors Card; existing holders can upgrade free.
benefits.value_text: Free upgrade; no $5 deposit (must load $5 credit)
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply online or call 13 74 68.

benefits.name: Seniors Business Discount Card
benefits.summary: A free discount card for Queenslanders aged 60+ who don't qualify for the full Seniors Card.
benefits.eligibility_text: Aged 60 or older and a Queensland resident (6+ months a year); not eligible for the Seniors Card.
benefits.value_text: Business discounts and Senior Shopper; no government concessions
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply through the same Seniors Card application.

benefits.name: Senior Shopper
benefits.summary: Free service that finds you a better price on appliances, cars, travel and discounted gift cards.
benefits.eligibility_text: Holders of a Seniors Card, Seniors Card +go or Seniors Business Discount Card.
benefits.value_text: Free service; gift cards about 2% to 11% off; average 26% saving on electrical goods (program claim)
benefits.how_to_claim: Register at seniorshopper.com.au and upload your card, then request a quote.

benefits.name: Seniors Card Interstate and New Zealand Discounts
benefits.summary: Use your Qld Seniors Card for business discounts interstate and with New Zealand SuperGold businesses.
benefits.eligibility_text: Queensland Seniors Card holders.
benefits.value_text: Discounts on request; varies by business
benefits.how_to_claim: Show your card and ask before purchasing; see the visited state's Seniors Card site or supergold.govt.nz.
benefits.notes: Government concessions are not included in the NZ arrangement.

benefits.name: Translink 50 Cent Fares (Seniors)
benefits.summary: All Translink bus, train, ferry and tram trips cost 50 cents for seniors.
benefits.eligibility_text: Seniors using a Senior go card or Seniors Card +go; all Translink fares are currently 50 cents for everyone.
benefits.value_text: 50 cents per journey
benefits.how_to_claim: Get a Senior go card (show Seniors Card) from a retailer, station or online, or upgrade to Seniors Card +go.
benefits.notes: 50c fares apply to all passengers now, so the seniors concession adds little on Translink. Regional non-Translink ferries accept any Australian Seniors Card. Gold Coast free bus travel ended 1 July 2025.

benefits.name: Brisbane Free Off-Peak Travel for Seniors
benefits.summary: Free off-peak trips on Brisbane City Council buses, CityCats and ferries.
benefits.eligibility_text: Seniors with a Senior go card or Seniors Card +go.
benefits.value_text: Free on Council buses weekdays 8:30am-3:30pm, 7pm-6am and weekends; CityCats/ferries weekdays off-peak only
benefits.how_to_claim: Touch on and off with your Senior go card.
benefits.notes: Not valid on Queensland Rail trains.

benefits.name: Long-Distance Rail Concession (Queensland Rail Travel)
benefits.summary: Up to half off long-distance Queensland Rail trains with a Seniors Card.
benefits.eligibility_text: Australian state Seniors Card (up to 50% off); interstate PCC (25% off); Queensland PCC holders get Queensland pensioner entitlements; Qld resident war widow/er Gold Card holders treated as Qld pensioners.
benefits.value_text: Up to 50% off adult fare (Seniors Card); 25% off (interstate PCC)
benefits.how_to_claim: Register your card on your Queensland Rail Travel profile then book online, or call.
benefits.notes: Page does not state the Queensland pensioner discount or any free-trip allowance. Meals and sleeper upgrades not discounted.

benefits.name: Vehicle Registration Concession
benefits.provider: Qld Department of Transport and Main Roads
benefits.summary: About half off the registration fee for one car or motorbike.
benefits.eligibility_text: Queensland resident with a Qld Seniors Card (not Business Discount Card) or Qld-issued PCC, or ADF member with 70% incapacity / 50 impairment points. One vehicle per person, one per spousal couple, private use, registered in your name.
benefits.value_text: About 50% off the registration fee, e.g. $385.45 to $192.75 for a 4-cylinder car (saves $192.70); CTP and traffic improvement fee not discounted
benefits.how_to_claim: Complete form F3937 and email, post or lodge it at a transport customer service centre with a copy of your card.
benefits.notes: Saving depends on vehicle; fee table at https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/registration/fees/cost. CSHC not listed. DVA Gold Card holders qualify only via TPI/EDA embossing or DVA letter.

benefits.name: Boat Registration Concession
benefits.provider: Qld Department of Transport and Main Roads
benefits.summary: Reduced registration fee for one private recreational boat.
benefits.eligibility_text: Queensland resident with Qld Seniors Card or Qld PCC (or prescribed ADF service person); recreational boat in your name; one boat per person, one concession per couple.
benefits.value_text: Reduced registration fee (see fee table)
benefits.how_to_claim: Complete form F3937 with a copy of your card; applies from the next registration period.
benefits.notes: Dollar amount not stated on page.

benefits.name: Taxi Subsidy Scheme
benefits.provider: Qld Department of Transport and Main Roads
benefits.summary: Half of your taxi fare paid, up to $30 a trip, if a severe disability stops you using public transport.
benefits.eligibility_text: Permanent Qld resident who uses a wheelchair, has a severe walking problem, severe vision loss, uncontrolled epilepsy, or dementia/intellectual impairment needing a companion.
benefits.value_text: 50% of the fare, up to $30 per trip, no trip limit
benefits.how_to_claim: Complete form QF2330 with a health professional and photo, then email or post to the Taxi Subsidy Unit.

benefits.name: Free Ambulance for Queensland Residents
benefits.summary: Ambulance treatment and transport is free for Queenslanders, including interstate.
benefits.eligibility_text: Queensland residents (principal place of residence in Qld) and their dependants.
benefits.value_text: Free; no ambulance cover needed
benefits.how_to_claim: Nothing to claim. If you get an interstate ambulance bill, follow the Qld interstate ambulance process.
benefits.notes: Not limited to pensioners.

benefits.name: Public Dental Services
benefits.summary: Free public dental care for adults with a concession card or Qld Seniors Card.
benefits.eligibility_text: Queensland residents with a PCC (Centrelink or DVA), Health Care Card, Commonwealth Seniors Health Card or Queensland Seniors Card.
benefits.value_text: Free (you pay your own transport)
benefits.how_to_claim: Contact your local public dental clinic to check eligibility and join the waiting list.
benefits.notes: Waiting lists apply.

benefits.name: Spectacle Supply Scheme
benefits.summary: Free basic prescription glasses every two years.
benefits.eligibility_text: Permanent Qld resident who has held a PCC, Health Care Card or Qld Seniors Card in their own name for 6 months; optometrist confirms your eyesight has changed.
benefits.value_text: Free basic glasses every 2 years
benefits.how_to_claim: Ask a participating optometrist; complete the MASS consent form.
benefits.notes: Confirm current details; page dated 2018.

benefits.name: Medical Aids Subsidy Scheme (MASS)
benefits.summary: Subsidised mobility, continence, daily-living and other aids for people with a permanent condition.
benefits.eligibility_text: Permanent Qld resident with a permanent, stable condition or disability, holding a PCC (Centrelink or DVA), Health Care Card or Qld Seniors Card; clinical assessment by an approved prescriber.
benefits.value_text: Aids on loan or supplied; value varies
benefits.how_to_claim: A clinician assesses you and applies (MASS-eApply).
benefits.notes: Card list from seniors health-subsidies page (2017); MASS page itself does not list cards. Copayment rules not confirmed.

benefits.name: Patient Travel Subsidy Scheme
benefits.summary: Help with travel and accommodation costs if you must travel far for specialist treatment.
benefits.eligibility_text: Queensland resident referred to a public specialist service not available locally, more than 50 km from your nearest public hospital.
benefits.value_text: Private car $0.45/km; commercial accommodation up to $70/night; private accommodation $10/night; approved escort may be covered
benefits.how_to_claim: Register and claim through your local hospital's PTSS office.
benefits.notes: No different rate for concession card holders stated.

benefits.name: Stocked Impoundment Permit Concession (Fishing)
benefits.summary: Cheaper annual permit to fish in stocked dams and weirs.
benefits.eligibility_text: Holders of a Qld Seniors Card, PCC, Health Care Card or Gold Card.
benefits.value_text: Concession annual permit $46.45 (standard $64.58)
benefits.how_to_claim: Buy online or from a permit agent and enter your card details.
benefits.notes: Queensland has no general recreational fishing licence; this permit is only needed in stocked impoundments. Saving $18.13 a year.
